D021-D013_h001.question:
I work nights at a data center, so my schedule’s pretty messed up, and over the last few months I’ve gotten really caught up in controlling what I eat. I started tracking everything, trying to “optimize” my energy, and it’s kind of spiraled. Now I’m down to what I know is a really low amount of calories a day. If I go over that number I feel anxious, like I’ve messed up.

I’ve been steadily losing weight. People at work comment that I look thinner, and my clothes are looser. Part of me notices that and thinks I should probably stop, but I keep tightening the rules anyway. I avoid things like pizza, burgers, anything I think is “heavy,” because I’m worried that if I eat them I’ll put on weight really fast, like it’ll show up the next day.

At the same time, my mood’s been off. I feel kind of flat and tired a lot, like I’m just going through the motions—work, home, sleep. I don’t really feel like hanging out with friends anymore, and even stuff I used to enjoy just feels sort of pointless.
D021-D013_h001.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
D021-D013_h001.answer: C & B. Anorexia Nervosa & Major Depressive Disorder

D021-D013_h002.question:
I guess this has been going on… maybe a couple of months? It’s a bit blurry. I just don’t feel like eating much. I’ll make something, then after a bite or two I’m done. At work, I’ll push food around during lunch with the other appraisers, maybe nibble on a cracker, and say I ate earlier. Most days it’s like that for every meal—just tiny portions.

I’ve noticed my clothes getting looser, my watch sliding around my wrist more. The scale keeps creeping down, and part of me notices that and part of me just… doesn’t want to think about it too hard. I do catch myself second‑guessing certain foods, especially anything that feels “heavy” or rich—pastries they bring into the lab, creamy pastas. I worry that if I eat them I’ll feel awful afterward, like it’ll show up on me right away, so it’s just easier to avoid them.

Along with all that, my mood’s been pretty low. I feel flat, tired, and it’s hard to get excited about anything, even pieces I used to love examining. I can do my job, but it feels like I’m moving through molasses most days.
D021-D013_h002.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
D021-D013_h002.answer: C & B. Anorexia Nervosa & Major Depressive Disorder

D021-D013_h003.question:

I work from home doing voice gigs, so my schedule is all over the place. At some point I started cutting out certain foods—first bread and pasta, then pretty much anything that feels “heavy” or greasy. I tell myself it’s just to feel lighter in my body and more “in control,” but now I get really anxious even thinking about eating things like pizza or desserts. It’s like I can almost feel them turning into weight on me right away, which sounds irrational, but it really freaks me out.

I’ve been eating smaller portions, skipping meals when I’m busy, and the number on the scale keeps going down. People have commented that I look thinner. I keep telling them I’m just “eating cleaner,” but I know I’m being pretty strict with myself.

At the same time, my mood’s been low. I’m tired a lot, even when I sleep in, and it’s harder to get excited about auditions or recording sessions. Some days I just sit there staring at my script, feeling sort of flat and unmotivated, and I end up nibbling on something small instead of making a real meal.
D021-D013_h003.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
D021-D013_h003.answer: C & B. Anorexia Nervosa & Major Depressive Disorder

D021-D013_h004.question:

At some point I decided I “needed to be more disciplined,” and I’ve gotten really strict with what I eat. I’ve cut out pretty much all bread, pasta, rice, and anything that feels “heavy” or greasy. If the number goes up even a tiny bit, I get this knot in my stomach and start replaying everything I ate that day, wondering what I did “wrong.”

D021-D013_h005.question:

I’ll skip breakfast because I want to get straight into a draft, then by the time I look up it’s late afternoon and I’ll just have coffee instead of lunch. If the number goes up even a little, I feel this rush of panic and start planning how to “make up for it” the next day. It’s on my mind a lot more than I’d like to admit.

A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D021-D013_h006.question:

D021-D013_h007.question:
I’d say this really started maybe a couple of months ago, though my wife thinks it’s been longer. I just don’t feel like eating much. The doctor and my family keep saying I’m losing weight too quickly, but I feel like they’re making a bigger deal of it than it is. I can still do my job, I still get through the day.

What bothers me more is this sort of low mood hanging over me. I’m more tired, not really excited about things I used to enjoy, and I catch myself just sitting there after work, staring at nothing. It’s not constant, but it’s there enough that my wife pushed me to come in.

A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa

D021-D013_h008.question:

D021-D013_h009.question:

    C. Anorexia Nervosa

D021-D013_h010.question:

D021-D013_h023.question:
I’ve been feeling off for maybe a couple of months now, it’s hard to pin down exactly. Working nights in the ER, I just… stopped really eating regular meals. I’ll grab a yogurt or a couple of bites of something and feel like that’s enough. If I sit down with a full plate, I get uncomfortable and push most of it around, maybe take a bite or two and then lose interest. Part of it is that I don’t like the idea of putting on any weight; even a small change on the scale makes me anxious, so it’s easier to just keep things “light.”

I’ve noticed my scrubs getting loose, my period’s been irregular, I get dizzy during long shifts, and my hair seems thinner when I put it up. But I just tell myself it’s stress, bad hospital coffee, and weird hours. Emotionally, I do feel more drained than usual, kind of flat and disconnected, like I’m on autopilot. On my days off I mostly stay in, don’t really feel like seeing friends or doing much. But I can still get through my shifts, so I keep telling myself it’s not that serious.
D021-D013_h023.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Delusional Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D021-D013_h023.answer: D & C. Anorexia Nervosa & Major Depressive Disorder

D021-D013_h024.question:
I’d say things started slipping maybe a few months ago, but it’s hard to pin down. I’ve just… lost interest in food. Most days I’ll pick at something so my husband doesn’t comment, like a few bites of salad or half a piece of toast, and I tell everyone I “ate earlier.” I feel better when my stomach is empty, lighter, more in control. The thought of putting on weight really bothers me, so I’m careful with portions and I check how my clothes fit a lot.

I’ve been more tired and flat, like someone turned the volume down on everything. Work used to excite me—colors, textures, planning spaces—but now I feel numb, going through the motions with clients. I have less patience with myself, feel guilty if I’m not “disciplined,” with work and with what I eat.

Physically, I get dizzy if I stand up too fast, my hair seems thinner, and my periods have been irregular, but I keep brushing it off as stress or hormones. I don’t really want to make a fuss about it; it feels like it’s not serious enough to worry anyone.
D021-D013_h024.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Delusional Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D021-D013_h024.answer: D & C. Anorexia Nervosa & Major Depressive Disorder

D021-D013_h025.question:
I’ve always been on the smaller side, and since my husband passed a couple of years ago my appetite just hasn’t really come back to what it was. Over the last… maybe six months or so, I’ve been cutting back more. I’ve stopped eating bread and pasta and most things with oil or butter. They just feel “too heavy” to me, and I don’t like the idea of putting that on my body at my age. I don’t weigh myself often, but I really don’t want to go up a size; the thought of getting bigger just makes me uncomfortable.

My daughter keeps saying I look “frail” and that I should eat more, but I don’t see it that way. I get around fine, I do my own shopping and gardening, so I don’t think it’s some big health crisis like they’re making it out to be.

Mood-wise, I do feel low a lot of days, and it’s hard to find much pleasure in things I used to enjoy. Sometimes I’m just tired and not very interested in food or going out, but I’m not sure if that’s just getting old and being on my own.
D021-D013_h025.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Delusional Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D021-D013_h025.answer: D & C. Anorexia Nervosa & Major Depressive Disorder
